config.title: Typing Uncertain Output

intro.title: Typing Uncertain Output
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple TypeScript function that handles uncertain or optional data, like a user profile that might be missing some information. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's union types to explicitly declare when a value could be of multiple types, such as a string or undefined. The main constructs involved are type annotations and union types (using the | operator). This will help you write safer, more predictable code by telling TypeScript exactly what to expect from your functions.
intro.usecase: Typing uncertain output is essential for handling data from APIs, user inputs, or external libraries where values might be missing or unknown. In real-world applications, this pattern appears in dashboards that fetch live data (e.g., stock prices or sensor readings that could be null), forms with optional fields, or search filters that return partial results. By properly typing these uncertain outputs, developers can build more robust and predictable UIs, preventing runtime errors and improving user experience in products like e-commerce platforms, analytics tools, or content management systems.

objectives: Implement union types to handle functions that return multiple possible data types
Apply type guards to narrow down union types within conditional logic
Construct functions that safely handle uncertain return values using optional chaining
Configure type assertions to override TypeScript's inference when you have more context
Initialize variables with the `unknown` type to enforce type checking before usage
Manipulate data from external APIs by applying proper typing for uncertain responses
Integrate error handling patterns that account for typed uncertain outcomes

steps.instruction: Add an explicit return type annotation to the 'getResult' function using the union type 'string | null'.

steps.title: Create interface for uncertain data structure
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'UserData' that describes an object with three properties: 'id' (required number), 'name' (required string), and 'email' (optional string).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Mark optional properties with a '?' after the property name.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named UserData with required id (number), required name (string), and optional email (string) properties.
successCriteria: The UserData interface is defined with correct property types and optional modifier.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all three properties are defined with correct types and the email property is marked as optional.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface isn't defined correctly. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword, named it 'UserData', and included all required properties with proper types.

successCriteria: The 'userData' object is defined with properties matching your interface, and at least one property is intentionally undefined or omitted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create type guard function
steps.instruction: Create a type guard function named 'isString' that takes a value of type unknown and returns a type predicate to check if it's a string.
steps.hint: Type guard functions use a return type annotation like 'value is string' to help TypeScript narrow types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a type guard function that can check if an unknown value is a string.
successCriteria: The 'isString' function is defined with proper type predicate return type and type checking logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has the correct return type annotation 'value is string' and checks the type properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The type guard function isn't quite right. It should take an unknown value and return a boolean with a type predicate.

steps.title: Implement conditional logic with uncertain output
steps.instruction: Write a function named 'processResult' that uses conditional logic to handle the uncertain return type from 'getResult'. The function should take a boolean parameter 'isValid', call 'getResult' with it, and return a descriptive string based on whether the result is a string or null.
steps.hint: Call 'getResult' inside your new function, then use an if statement or ternary to check if the result is a string (you can use the 'isString' type guard) and return different messages accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new function 'processResult' that demonstrates conditional handling of uncertain types by returning different messages based on the type of output from 'getResult'.
successCriteria: The 'processResult' function is defined, takes a boolean parameter, calls 'getResult', uses conditional logic (if/else or ternary) with the 'isString' type guard, and returns appropriate string messages for both string and null cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function: 1) Takes a boolean parameter, 2) Calls 'getResult', 3) Uses conditional logic with 'isString', and 4) Returns appropriate messages for both cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't meet the requirements. Make sure to create a function named 'processResult' that handles the uncertain output from 'getResult' using conditional logic with the 'isString' type guard.

steps.title: Use optional chaining with uncertain data
steps.instruction: In your existing code, add a new function called 'getUserName' that safely accesses the 'name' property of the 'userData' object using optional chaining (?.) and returns the result.
steps.hint: Optional chaining allows you to safely access nested properties without throwing an error if any part of the chain is undefined. Use the syntax: object?.property
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll create a function that demonstrates safe property access on potentially undefined data using optional chaining.
successCriteria: The 'getUserName' function is defined and uses optional chaining (?.) to access the 'name' property of 'userData'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using optional chaining (?.) to access the 'name' property of 'userData' in your function.

steps.title: Implement nullish coalescing for fallback values
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'getUserName' that uses the nullish coalescing operator (??) to provide a fallback value when the user's name is undefined or null.
steps.hint: The nullish coalescing operator returns the right-hand side only when the left-hand side is null or undefined. You can use it to provide a default string like 'Guest'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that demonstrates how to use the nullish coalescing operator to handle uncertain values by providing a default fallback.
successCriteria: The getUserName function uses the nullish coalescing operator (??) to return a fallback string when the name is null or undefined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use the nullish coalescing operator (??) and provide a fallback string.
